candidate.answerReason: The strips have total area 40, with four separate unit-square crossings each counted twice. Subtracting one copy of each crossing gives 36.

methods.label: Remove the extra counts at the crossings
methods.explanation:
Adding the four strip areas counts the overlapping parts twice, so we must remove those extra counts. Each strip has area \(10\cdot1=10\), giving a total of \(40\) before correcting for overlap.

[Figure 1](figures/1988_AMC_12_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

Each of the two horizontal strips crosses each of the two vertical strips, making four separate crossings. Since the strips have width \(1\) and meet perpendicularly, every crossing is a \(1\) by \(1\) square of area \(1\). The horizontal strips do not overlap each other, and neither do the vertical strips, so no region belongs to three or four strips.

Every crossing was counted twice instead of once. Subtracting its area once corrects that duplication, while every other covered part remains counted once. The covered area is therefore
\[
4(10\cdot1)-4(1\cdot1)=40-4=36
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
